content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days.
- Model tends to lag behind true price movements in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–7 days).
- Overshoots in the middle of forecast (days 8–15) when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects after sharp price spikes, leading to premature declines.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days), especially when sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model delays the upward correction, causing lagged peak alignment.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend direction if sentiment shifts sharply — model often ignores sentiment reversal signals.
